summary: The Philippines admits citizens of the countries listed under Executive Order 408 visa-free for 30 days — extendable by 29 days at a Bureau of Immigration office — and requires every arriving traveler to register on the free eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival. Visa-free visitors must also hold a return or onward ticket.

fee.notes: Embassy in Washington, for nationals who need a visa: USD 40 single entry valid three months, USD 80 multiple entry for six months, USD 120 for one year (nationals of visa-free countries pay USD 30, 60 and 90; Chinese nationals USD 25, 50 and 100). e-Visa applications add a USD 25 convenience fee.

fee.notes: PHP 500 visa waiver fee, PHP 1,000 application fee, PHP 500 certification fee, PHP 30 legal research fee and PHP 1,000 express fee, paid at a Bureau of Immigration office (the BI dates this table 6 March 2014). Further monthly extensions are possible afterward, up to 36 months in total for visa-free nationals.

passportValidity.text: Your passport must be valid for at least 6 months beyond your intended stay in the Philippines.

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever vaccination certificate (ICVP) is required only if you arrive from, or transited through, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: WHO — International Travel and Health country list: vaccination requirements (Philippines)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel-insurance requirement for the Philippines. The UK Foreign Office advises making sure you have adequate travel health insurance and accessible funds to cover the cost of any medical treatment, including repatriation.

source.name: UK FCDO — the Philippines travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for proof of it.

source.name: Department of Foreign Affairs — Philippine visa policy (eVisaPH)

proofOfFunds.text: No official source we could read states a general proof-of-funds requirement or amount for the Philippines. The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy asks Indian nationals entering visa-free for 14 days to show proof of financial capacity.

source.name: Department of Foreign Affairs — Philippine visa policy (eVisaPH)

declarations.name: eTravel Registration
declarations.text: Every traveler arriving in the Philippines (foreigners and Filipinos alike) must register on the eTravel platform within 72 hours before arrival and present the QR code at check-in and immigration. It is completely free. Use only etravel.gov.ph.

source.name: eTravel — Frequently Asked Questions

currencyLimits.text: Foreign currency over 10,000 USD (or equivalent) must be declared on arrival and departure. Bringing in or taking out more than 50,000 PHP in Philippine currency requires prior authorization from the central bank (BSP).

source.name: Bureau of Customs — e-Travel customs declaration and BSP rules on bringing in or taking out currencies

notes: The UK government says there are strict rules on goods taken into or out of the Philippines, and you must declare anything that may be prohibited or subject to tax or duty.

The Bureau of Customs says all arriving passengers fill in the electronic Customs Baggage Declaration Form (e-CBDF) on the eTravel website or the eGovPH app within 72 hours before arrival, and those carrying currency above the allowed threshold also fill in the electronic Currencies Declaration Form (e-CDF); the eTravel QR code is shown to the customs officer for clearance.

payments.text: No official source we checked describes card acceptance in the Philippines. Canada's travel advice says ATMs are available in larger cities but may be scarce in rural areas, and to make sure you have access to cash in local currency if you travel outside larger urban areas.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office advises against all travel to western and central Mindanao and the Sulu archipelago, and against all but essential travel to the rest of Mindanao except Camiguin, Dinagat and Siargao islands, because of terrorist activity and clashes between the military and insurgent groups in the south.

bestTimeToVisit.text: Canada's travel advice says the rainy season runs from May to November, though storms can occur all year, and the UK government says around 20 typhoons hit the Philippines each year, mostly between June and November. No official source names a best season; the months shown fall outside the rainy season.

idp.text: Philippines is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either.

driving.text: Philippines is a party to both the 1949 Geneva and the 1968 Vienna Conventions on Road Traffic, so it recognizes an International Driving Permit issued under either. The UK Foreign Office says you can drive on a UK driving licence for up to 90 days and must apply for a Philippine licence for longer stays; the Government of Canada says the same for a Canadian licence and advises carrying an International Driving Permit.

tips.text: Book an onward or return ticket before you fly: the Department of Foreign Affairs says visa-free visitors must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination, and the UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it.
Register only on the official eTravel portal, etravel.gov.ph.

After the initial 30 days, the Bureau of Immigration offers a first 29-day visa waiver, then further extensions of stay (in 1- or 2-month steps, or up to 6 months under the Long-Stay Visitor Extension); it gives 36 months as the maximum allowable stay for visa-free nationals.

The UK government says around 20 typhoons hit the Philippines each year, mostly between June and November, and Canada says authorities may suspend ferry services at short notice when a storm signal is raised, so you could be stranded at a port for days; Canada advises planning extra time for sea travel, especially in the rainy season.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No. US passport holders enter visa-free for up to 30 days with a passport valid 6 months and an onward ticket. The stay can be extended by 29 days (and beyond) at Bureau of Immigration offices. Everyone must also register on eTravel within 72 hours before arrival.

faq.question: What is eTravel and who needs it?
faq.answer: eTravel (etravel.gov.ph) is the Philippines' free online arrival registration combining immigration, health and customs declarations. Every arriving traveler — foreign or Filipino — must complete it within 72 hours before arrival and show the QR code at check-in and on arrival.

faq.question: Is an onward ticket really required for the Philippines?
faq.answer: Yes, for visa-free visitors. The Department of Foreign Affairs' visa policy says visa-free nationals must hold a return ticket to their country of origin or an outward-bound ticket to their next destination. The UK government says immigration officials and airlines may ask for it, and Canada says customs officials may ask to see a return or onward ticket.

faq.question: How do I extend my stay in the Philippines?
faq.answer: Apply at the Bureau of Immigration main office or another authorized immigration office before your current stay expires. The first step is a 29-day visa waiver (PHP 3,030); after that you can extend in 1- or 2-month steps, or up to 6 months under the Long-Stay Visitor Extension. The Bureau gives 36 months as the maximum allowable stay for visa-free nationals.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for the Philippines?
faq.answer: No, not for short visits. Indian passport holders can enter visa-free for 14 days for tourism or business (not extendable), with a passport valid 6 months beyond the stay, a confirmed hotel booking, proof of funds and a return or onward ticket. Those holding a valid US, UK, Schengen, Japanese, Australian, Canadian or Singapore visa or residence permit can instead stay 30 days for tourism, also not extendable. Longer stays need a temporary visitor (9a) visa.
